study_identification.author_journal_year: Fraza et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification.title: Unraveling the link between CNVs, cognition and individual neuroimaging deviation scores from a population-based reference cohort

study_characteristics.study_objective: To map individualized brain deviation scores in individuals with pathogenic copy number variations (CNVs) using normative modeling, examining the relationship between CNVs, brain structure, and cognitive function at the individual level. The study aims to quantify individual variations against population reference norms across various neuroimaging modalities and correlate these deviations with cognitive ability.

site_effect_handling.reason: Site was included as a fixed effect in the normative model to reduce site effects. The paper explicitly discusses this approach and contrasts it with harmonization procedures.
site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Every normative model constructed factored in the covariates age and sex. To reduce site effects, we have added it as a fixed effect in the model. In general, incorporating site as a confounding variable during the fitting procedure is the most effective approach for handling site effects. Harmonization procedures can also be considered, if the site data are unavailable or for adapting larger models afterward. However, they come with extensive drawbacks, including the potential removal of meaningful variance correlated with site effects.

This algorithm employed Sinarcsinh likelihood warping and Powell optimization. A cubic B-spline basis expansion with 5 evenly spaced knots was chosen.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.answer: Yes - The model appropriately handles multiple forms of nuisance structure including: (1) nonlinearity in age effects via B-spline basis functions, (2) non-Gaussianity via Sinarcsinh likelihood warping, (3) site effects via fixed-effect modeling, and (4) heteroscedasticity. Model performance was evaluated using kurtosis and skewness metrics to assess warping function effectiveness.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper demonstrates comprehensive handling of nuisance structure through multiple techniques: B-spline basis functions for age nonlinearity (5 knots chosen empirically to capture age-related curvature), likelihood warping to accommodate non-Gaussianity, and fixed-effect site modeling. Performance metrics (kurtosis, skewness) were used to validate proper handling of non-Gaussian distributions. All voxels showed relatively low skew (|skew| <1) and acceptable excess kurtosis (<5), indicating successful warping.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: To ensure accurate modeling of nonlinear and non-Gaussian effects, we employed a B-spline basis function and likelihood warping, as described in ref. 38. A cubic B-spline basis expansion with 5 evenly spaced knots was chosen. Empirically, this was enough to capture the curvature in space caused by the age covariate. The likelihood warping φ, a Sinarcsinh function, accommodates non-Gaussianity. Among these were the kurtosis and skewness of the resulting z-score distribution, which measures the effectiveness of the warping function in capturing the nonlinearity and non-Gaussianity of the data. In general, all voxels show relatively low skew (that is, |skew| <1) and acceptable excess kurtosis (<5). To reduce site effects, we have added it as a fixed effect in the model.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.location: Main text pages 4 and 8 (Methods); Supplement pages 7-8

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Spearman rank correlation between total count of extreme deviation scores and general cognitive ability (derived from principal component analysis of seven UK Biobank cognitive tests). Extreme positive deviations (z > 2) showed r=0.03, p=0.09 (not significant). Extreme negative deviations (z < -2) showed r=-0.04, p=0.04 (significant), indicating that higher numbers of extreme negative deviations (more volume contractions) were associated with lower general cognitive ability. Additional exploratory Spearman correlations were performed between deviation scores and other behavioral variables and polygenic scores for psychiatric disorders (ADHD, ASD, MDD, anxiety, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, cannabis use disorder) with FDR correction for multiple comparisons.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Individuals with pathogenic CNVs showed highly heterogeneous patterns of brain structural deviations from normative models, with negative deviations (volume contractions) significantly associated with lower cognitive ability (r=-0.04, p=0.04).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study mapped individualized brain deviation scores in 375 CNV carriers using voxel-wise normative models trained on 19,620 healthy individuals. Key findings include: (1) Structural measures showed greater variation in deviation scores compared to functional or diffusion measures, with models explaining up to 52% of variance. (2) High heterogeneity was observed among CNV carriers - for example, 1q21.1 duplication carriers (n=5) showed more negative deviations (volume contractions) reflecting macrocephaly, while deletion carriers (n=5) showed more positive deviations reflecting microcephaly, consistent with known dosage effects. (3) Specific brain regions showed marked deviations in certain individuals: cerebellum, brainstem, and pallidum for some 1q21.1 duplication carriers; caudate and accumbens for certain deletion carriers. (4) Aggregated analysis revealed convergent patterns across carriers: 1q21.1 duplication showed negative deviations in occipital cortex; deletion showed positive deviations in cerebellum and thalamus. (5) Negative deviations significantly correlated with lower general cognitive ability (r=-0.04, p=0.04), while positive deviations showed no significant correlation (r=0.03, p=0.09). (6) Similar patterns of heterogeneity were observed for other CNVs (15q11.2, 16p11.2, 16p13.11), demonstrating the versatility of the approach for studying rare genetic variants. The findings underscore individual-level variation in CNV effects and demonstrate that normative modeling can map brain impacts of rare variants beyond what group-level case-control studies can reveal.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Several important limitations were identified: (1) Lack of longitudinal imaging data, particularly in younger age ranges where CNV effects on neurodevelopment are most pronounced - the study was limited to older adults (46-80 years) from UK Biobank. (2) Individual deviation scores may be partly driven by effects outside the CNVs, including the remaining genome, environmental factors, and lifestyle factors that interact with genetic risk. (3) Disproportionate representation of individuals of European ancestry (>96% white in most cohorts) limits generalizability to diverse ancestral backgrounds. (4) Cannot establish causality or direction of effects - CNVs may be present in healthy individuals, and expression of associated disorders likely involves gene-environment interactions. (5) The study design is cross-sectional, preventing assessment of developmental trajectories or critical time windows. (6) Models were trained primarily on middle-to-older age adults, limiting ability to characterize effects during childhood and adolescence when neurodevelopmental impacts may be strongest.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The authors emphasize this study as a starting point toward personalized psychiatry and individual-level CNV profiling. They note that the normative modeling approach enables study of rare CNVs that would be difficult or impossible to examine with traditional case-control designs due to small sample sizes. The individual deviation maps can be used to identify convergence points among carriers with similar behavioral phenotypes while also revealing the heterogeneity of CNV effects. The authors caution against defaulting to case-control thinking when interpreting normative model outputs and emphasize that individual patient risk profiles should integrate multiple factors (genetics, environment, lifestyle) rather than relying solely on group-level patterns. Future work will integrate these models with longitudinal data and epigenetic pathways to understand gene-environment-brain interactions over developmental time. The code and models are made publicly available on GitHub to enable application to other rare genetic variants and datasets.

general_notes.general_notes: This is a methodological advancement paper demonstrating the application of normative modeling to study rare pathogenic copy number variations (CNVs) at the individual level. The study analyzed 92 pathogenic CNVs but focused detailed results on 1q21.1 distal deletion and duplication, with additional results for 15q11.2, 16p11.2, and 16p13.11 in supplementary materials. The paper used two complementary analysis approaches: (1) IDP-based analysis using 2,084 summary measures from UK Biobank (43,893 participants), and (2) voxel-wise Jacobian analysis using data pooled from five repositories with seven sites (19,620 participants total). The Jacobian determinants represent local volume expansion/contraction needed for registration to MNI152 space, with values >1 indicating expansion and <1 indicating contraction. In the normative model framework, positive deviations indicate more expansion than predicted (relatively smaller original volume), while negative deviations indicate more contraction than predicted (relatively larger original volume). The study received ethical approval through UK Biobank application 23668. Funding was provided by European Research Council grant 'MENTALPRECISION' 101001118 and Dutch Organisation for Scientific Research VIDI grant 016.156.415. One author (C.F.B.) declared being director and shareholder in SBGneuro Ltd. The full dataset demographics show diversity in ethnicity categories: UK Biobank samples were >96% white; HCP 76% white, 14% Black, 6% Asian; OASIS 3 84% white, 15% Black. The paper provides extensive supplementary materials including individual brain maps for all CNV carriers, correlation analyses with polygenic scores, and detailed mathematical formulations of the warped Bayesian linear regression approach.
